title: auth: scoped tokens, nonce header, and CORS updates for OpenAI-compatible API
author: Asha Patel
release_notes: Update auth header semantics for OpenAI-compatible endpoints: scoped token support, optional X-Nonce header for request signing, and clarified CORS policy for project/org keys. Backwards-compatible for most customers; recommended config changes for private deployments.
description:
Summary: This PR standardizes authorization header semantics across the OpenAI-compatibility layer and API surface: 1) explicit support for scoped tokens (project/org-scoped API keys) and clearer precedence rules; 2) optional X-Nonce header to support signed short-lived requests and mitigate replay; 3) tightened CORS response headers for project-level keys while preserving developer UX for user-level keys. Motivation: multiple customers and internal integration tests surfaced ambiguous header precedence (Authorization vs X-Project-Key vs X-Org-Key), inconsistent behavior for scoped tokens during routing, and a replay vector in some proxying setups. This change makes semantics explicit, improves streaming stability when auth tokens are validated at the edge, and provides a signing primitive for integrations that require request nonce verification.

What changed (high level):
- API gatekeeper (gateway/auth middleware): added comprehensive header parsing and precedence rules. Order of precedence is now: 1) Authorization: Bearer <token> (explicit token), 2) X-Project-Key, 3) X-Org-Key, 4) legacy X-Api-Key (deprecated). If multiple are present, middleware returns 400 with a clear error message unless the token and project/org key are the same owner (used in service-to-service handoffs).
- Scoped tokens: token introspection endpoint and middleware now surface scope claims ("scope": ["project:read","project:write","org:admin"]) and enforce endpoint-level ACLs for tool/function-calling and structured-output endpoints.
- X-Nonce header: optional header accepted by the gateway for signed requests. When present, gateway validates nonce using tenant-specific replay caches and signature timestamp window (default 60s). Middleware emits metric auth.nonce.accepted/rejected.
- CORS: project-scoped keys used from browser contexts are constrained. Responses will include Access-Control-Allow-Origin only if the origin matches a configured allowlist for the project or if the request is using a user-scoped token. Explicitly documented behavior to avoid accidental exposure for org keys.
- OpenAI-compat layer: updated to map incoming OpenAI-style Authorization semantics into Redwood auth model without dropping nonce or scope metadata. Streaming handlers updated to forward validated auth context consistently to downstream runtime nodes to fix intermittent streaming disconnects observed when auth was validated asynchronously at the edge.

Files touched (selected):
- gateway/auth/middleware.go (Go): added header parser, precedence logic, nonce validation hook, and tests.
- gateway/auth/introspect_client.go (Go): expanded token introspection response handling to include scope claims and home_project/home_org identifiers.
- api/openai/compatibility/auth_adapter.py (Python): adapter layer to translate OpenAI Authorization headers into Redwood internal claims, preserve nonce, and raise clear errors for conflicting headers.
- docs/openai-compat/auth.md: updated semantics and examples for scoped tokens, browser usage, and migration notes.
- docs/upgrade-notes/2026-02-auth-key-semantics.md: operator guidance for private deployments (KMS signing keys + replay cache upgrade).
- runtime/streaming/handler.cpp: minor fix to ensure auth context is attached to the streaming session before first chunk is dispatched.
- test/integration/auth_scoped_tokens_test.go, test/integration/auth_nonce_test.go: new integration tests covering precedence, replay detection, and scope enforcement on function-calling endpoints.

Small illustrative snippets (not exhaustive):
- Go precedence pseudocode:
  func resolveAuth(headers) (principal, err) {
    // precedence: Authorization > X-Project-Key > X-Org-Key > X-Api-Key
    if auth := headers.Get("Authorization"); auth != "" { return inspectToken(auth) }
    if pk := headers.Get("X-Project-Key"); pk != "" { return lookupProjectKey(pk) }
    if ok := headers.Get("X-Org-Key"); ok != "" { return lookupOrgKey(ok) }
    if legacy := headers.Get("X-Api-Key"); legacy != "" { log.Warn("deprecated header"); return lookupLegacy(legacy) }
    return nil, ErrNoAuth
  }

- Nonce sample validation (Python adapter):
  if headers.get("X-Nonce"):
      if not validate_nonce(headers["X-Nonce"], token_owner):
          raise AuthError("replay or invalid nonce")

Commits (summary):
- feat(auth): add header precedence and scoped token introspection (Asha Patel)
- feat(auth): add nonce validation and replay cache support (Marco Alvarez)
- fix(streaming): attach auth context to streaming sessions (Sofia Chen)
- docs: add migration guide and examples (TBD)

Tests & CI: All unit and integration tests added. CI runs updated: auth unit tests (go/python), integration suite, and e2e streaming canary. One rerun was necessary after a flake in the streaming canary; final CI status: pass.

Review conversation (high level):
- Jordan Kim (reviewer): Asked for explicit error behavior when multiple auth headers are present. Requested unit tests for precedence and a clear error string for SDK teams. "Please make the error machine-parseable (json code + message) so SDKs can surface it." Author responded with a follow-up commit adding a structured error and tests.
- Marco Alvarez (reviewer): Requested metrics around nonce rejections and a configurable window for replay protection. Implemented by adding config keys: auth.nonce.window_seconds and auth.nonce.cache_ttl.
- Sofia Chen (reviewer): Found a race in streaming session attachment during heavy load. Proposed a mutex in the session bootstrap path, which was applied with a micro-benchmark showing no measurable latency regression.
- Security review (automated + manual): Recommended tightening CORS defaults for project keys; documentation updated with examples and operator guidance.

Backward compatibility & migration notes:
- Most customers unaffected. Legacy X-Api-Key remains supported but is marked deprecated and emits a telemetry flag.
- Operators running private deployments must update their replay cache storage (Redis cluster) to a supported version or enable in-memory fallback (not recommended). See docs/upgrade-notes/2026-02-auth-key-semantics.md.
- SDKs: small surface change where structured auth errors may be returned for multiple conflicting headers; SDKs should surface the error code and the suggested fix.

Merge outcome: PR merged via squash on 2026-02-25 after approvals from Jordan, Marco, and Sofia. Release notes drafted for the 2026-03 minor release. Monitoring: added dashboards auth.nonce.rejections and auth.header.conflicts; alert configured for >10 conflicts / minute.

If you need the exact diff for any file, ping me; kept changes focused to auth adapters, gateway middleware, streaming context plumbing, docs, and tests.
notes: Squash merge. Coordinated with SDK teams for a small follow-up to surface structured errors in client libraries. Ops informed for Redis replay cache sizing.
